attachments.origin_landmark: lesser wing of the sphenoid, above the optic canal
attachments.insertion_landmark: skin and tarsal plate of the upper eyelid

innervation.root_levels: CN III (with sympathetic supply to the superior tarsal muscle)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Dual supply is what makes ptosis diagnostic: CN III palsy gives complete ptosis, whereas loss of the sympathetic supply to the smooth superior tarsal (Muller's) muscle within it gives the partial ptosis of Horner syndrome.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: origin (lesser wing of the sphenoid, above the optic canal)
motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: insertion (tarsal plate and skin of the upper eyelid)
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The oculomotor branch typically wraps around the medial border of superior rectus (78.6% of specimens) before entering LPS's inferior surface; its tree-like intramuscular sub-branches concentrate within the proximal two-thirds of the muscle (this 0-67% band, counted from the origin), though thin retrograde twigs can extend as far as the insertion. This favors placing an injection posteriorly/proximally when the goal is to weaken the whole muscle uniformly.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Haladaj R, Wysiadecki G, Tubbs RS, Topol M, 'Anatomical variations of the levator palpebrae superioris, including observations on its innervation and intramuscular nerves' distribution pattern', Ann Anat 228:151439 (2020), doi:10.1016/j.aanat.2019.151439 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aanat.2019.151439) -- 70 orbits, Sihler staining -- retrieved via PubMed

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound or EMG technique in real practice -- guidance is by direct anatomic visualization. Classic technique: percutaneous/transcutaneous injection through the mid-upper-eyelid skin, 2-3mm above the lash line in the eyelid crease, needle angled toward the superior orbit and advanced 12-15mm to reach LPS anterior to the orbital septum. Modern, complication-reducing technique: the upper lid is double-everted over a Desmarres retractor and the toxin is injected trans-conjunctivally at the superior edge of Muller's muscle, where it lies immediately adjacent to LPS.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Anterior orbit/eyelid, superficial to the orbital septum for the transcutaneous route; sub-conjunctival, just deep to Muller's muscle, for the trans-conjunctival route.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: No electrical or sonographic confirmation is used; correct placement is inferred from surface landmarks (eyelid crease, superior tarsal border) and from the resulting ptosis, which develops over 2-5 days.
structures_at_risk: superior rectus, which the transcutaneous approach risks paretically involving if the injection tracks too posteriorly/deep -- the main reason the trans-conjunctival technique was developed
Muller's (superior tarsal) muscle -- unaffected by a purely transcutaneous injection, which is why lagophthalmos/incomplete ptosis is more common with that route
globe, if the needle is advanced too deep during the transcutaneous approach
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Used clinically to create a deliberate, reversible 'protective ptosis' covering the cornea in exposure keratopathy, neurotrophic ulcers, and facial-palsy-related lagophthalmos -- not for strabismus. This is one of the few extraocular botulinum indications where EMG guidance is NOT used at all; guidance is anatomic/visual.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Tint NL, Saxby EPI, Young SL, Alexander P, 'A modified transconjunctival technique for botulinum toxin chemodenervation of levator palpebrae superioris for corneal protection', Eye (Lond) 36(6):1217-1221 (2022), doi:10.1038/s41433-021-01587-x (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41433-021-01587-x) -- 21 patients, PMC9151670; Naik MN, Gangopadhyay N, Fernandes M, Murthy R, Honavar SG, 'Anterior chemodenervation of levator palpebrae superioris with botulinum toxin type-A (Botox) to induce temporary ptosis for corneal protection', Eye (Lond) 22(9):1132-1136 (2007), doi:10.1038/sj.eye.6702866 (https://doi.org/10.1038/sj.eye.6702866) -- 10 eyes, classic transcutaneous technique -- both retrieved via PubMed
